text:
Mia Chen: quick q — building the 'create experiment' flow in Console, wondering what we want as the default canary split. 1% or 5%? :thinking:
Omar Patel: i'd vote 1% by default for risky infra changes, but 5% is more useful for signal on small models.
Lucy Park: UX-wise 1% is safer, but we should show an inline tip about minimum samples needed for metrics.
Mia Chen: agree. also debating whether the Console should auto-create a monitoring hook for rollout metrics (latency, error_rate) when user doesn't pick one.
Raj Singh: auto-creating hooks is handy but could be noisy. Maybe auto-create but set retention to 7d and mark as "suggested" not enforced.
Taylor Nguyen: from API side, POST /v1/experiments currently requires `metrics: []`. We can make it optional and Console will patch with defaults. Example payload we discussed:
```
POST /v1/experiments
{
  "name": "shiny-feature-canary",
  "variants": [
    {"id": "ctrl", "weight": 9900},
    {"id": "canary", "weight": 100}
  ],
  "routing_policy": "user-id-hash",
  "metrics": null
}
```
Omar Patel: that patch behavior is fine but make sure the API records who created defaults (console vs user) for audit.
deploy-bot: experiment shiny-feature-canary created by @Mia Chen (id: exp_0b123)
Lucy Park: UI idea: when user picks variant weights, show an inline estimator: "est. requests/day per variant" based on recent traffic. Helps avoid tiny buckets.
Mia Chen: yes, and for quotas/guards: do we want to enforce per-variant QPS caps at creation or let ops add them later?
Raj Singh: enforce sensible upper bounds (e.g., cannot exceed account's dedicated capacity) but allow user to opt-out. Otherwise users can accidentally DDoS their own model.
Taylor Nguyen: technical note — our routing service expects seed weighting as 0..1 floats. Console sends ints currently. We'll add a normalization layer in the SDK.
Omar Patel: also edge case: if a model rollout falls back to lower-capacity region, the routing policy should auto-fallback to 'regional-compat' variant mapping. Need a rule in experiment config like `fallback_policy: preserve-proportions | promote-control`.
Lucy Park: UX wants that as a toggle: "Preserve split if fallback happens" vs "Send all to control" with short descriptions.
Mia Chen: telemetry naming convention: use `experiment.<exp_id>.<variant_id>.(latency|error|ctr)` so downstream dashboards can roll up. Agree?
Raj Singh: agreed. Also emit `experiment.assignment_seed` and `routing_reason` (explicit route vs fallback) as fields.
Taylor Nguyen: implementation plan: Console creates experiment, sends normalized variant weights + optional default metrics + suggested monitoring hook, API tags defaults with `created_by=console` and `defaulted=true`. Rollout service reads `fallback_policy`.
Omar Patel: one more: can we have a lightweight "preview" mode in Console that simulates 10k pseudo-requests against the chosen routing (using your site's observed hash distribution) so product teams can see allocation?
Lucy Park: love it. let's add a small notice: "Preview uses sampled traffic; not a guarantee." :sparkles:
Mia Chen: ok action items: Taylor to add normalization + tags on API; Raj to propose guard upper bounds doc; Lucy to mock preview UI; Omar to draft fallback_policy enum semantics. I'll wire the telemetry names.
Raj Singh: ack, will post a short RFC by EOD tomorrow.
Taylor Nguyen: ack, will aim for PR with tests by Friday.
Mia Chen: thanks team :thumbsup:
